issues.summary: restoreWeekFromHealBackup_ deletes EVERY live Summary row for the week (predicate is week alone, Code.gs:1979) but re-appends only the snapshot-once baseline frozen at the week's FIRST heal. Pull-owned rows written to Summary AFTER that baseline -- shopify_orderapp online revenue (orderapp.gs writes Summary directly; PRD-10) and Labour -- are in neither the snapshot nor any recompute, so the restore destroys them with no recovery path. Confirmed by probe: a $4,321.55 shopify_orderapp row went 1 -> 0 rows and restore reported success ({restored:1}). This is the same (week)-only-predicate hazard mayers.gs:505 documents as able to destroy the ~$14,219 Bennetts row permanently. Only partially mitigated: shopifyWeeklyPull re-pulls the last 4 completed weeks, so a restore of an older week is unrecoverable. Fix: exclude pull-owned rows (shopify_orderapp / Labour) from the delete loop, as healOrphanCandidates_ and summaryOrphanSweep_ already do. No test seeds a pull-owned row before a restore.

The step9 FIX1 empty-baseline marker reintroduces the exact ambiguous signal step7's CRITICAL FIX1 was written to eliminate. A marker-only snapshot passes the non-empty/validity guards, so restoreWeekFromHealBackup_ deletes all live rows and returns {restored:0} -- indistinguishable from the benign no-op that fix banned. Confirmed by probe: 1 live row -> 0 rows, returned {"week":"2026-08-03","restored":0}. Compounding it, listSummaryHealBackups() counts the marker as a restorable row and reports rows:1, total:$0, so the operator's documented pre-flight view says there IS something to restore for a week whose restore means 'delete everything'. Return a distinct outcome (e.g. restoredToEmptyBaseline) and exclude markers from the listing count.

weeklySummarize() returns two incompatible shapes switched by the SUMMARY_HEAL_ENABLED Script Property (weeklySummarize_impl_:2437-2472). Confirmed by probe -- flag OFF: {weekStart, weekEnd, summariesAdded, summariesUpdated, labourTabAdded, labourSummaryAdded}; flag ON: {weeks, success, newestWeekFailed, weekStart, weekEnd}, where summariesAdded is undefined. Two consequences: (a) the repo's documented undefined+undefined=NaN failure class is reachable by any consumer or manual probe reading the count fields; (b) the multi-week shape omits `refused` entirely, so the established completion test used by greenBeanPull_ (orderapp.gs:947, `if (sumRes && !sumRes.refused)`) reads an all-weeks-refused run as success. Live callers pass an explicit week today so nothing breaks yet, but the flag is designed to be turned on. Carry refused/success consistently across both shapes.

In raiseCalendarAlert_, setColor()/setDescription() run after createAllDayEvent() inside one try block, and stalenessResolveColor_ falls back to returning the raw string for an unknown key. An unrecognised color name therefore creates the event, throws on setColor, and returns 0 -- leaving an orphaned all-day event with no description while the caller records 'no alert raised' and the events cache is never updated. Resolve/validate the color before creating the event.

healWeeks_ seeds backedUpWeeks with `backedUpWeeks[coerceDateStr_(r[0])] = true` and omits the DATE_ARG_RE guard that previewSummaryHeal, summaryOrphanSweep_ and listSummaryHealBackups (step9 FIX5) all apply to the same class of read. A blank/malformed backup date seeds a '' key. Harmless today because '' cannot collide with a real week_start, but it is the one remaining instance of the pattern step9 FIX5 set out to close.

The Labour correction alert builds its event title from the joined list of healed weeks (weeklySummarize_impl_, `labourWeeks.map(...).join(', ')` passed as the `week` argument to healRaiseAlert_). raiseCalendarAlert_ documents the title as the within-day idempotency key and explicitly requires callers to keep it stable with no varying date in it; this title changes whenever the healed-week set changes. Low impact on a weekly trigger, but it violates the contract the same commit introduced.
